headline: Liberia Lands the First Twenty
deck: A plane carrying 20 third-country transferees from the United States arrived at Roberts International on Thursday, matching the date the information ministry had set on 18 August. No new Liberian landing communiqué was on the site at the freeze.
body: The Ministry of Information said on 18 August that the first batch of 20 people under Liberia’s arrangement with the United States would arrive on Thursday, 20 August, at Roberts International Airport [E1]. Those people are third-country nationals, some of whom may seek asylum in Liberia, and the government said they are not criminals and are not being prosecuted under US or Liberian law [E1]. The cap remains 1,200 within a year, on an exchange of notes dated 4 and 10 September 2025 [E1]. Thursday is the date that announcement named [E1].

A plane carrying the group arrived at Roberts on 20 August [E2]. Associated Press described 20 deportees landing outside Monrovia and photographed the aircraft on Thursday [E2]. Justice Minister Natu Oswald Tweh said they could seek asylum if they wished [E2]. Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah placed the nationalities in a broad band of African and Western Hemisphere countries [E2]. Names of the 20 were not published [E1][E2].

The US side did not confirm the specific flight. The State Department called implementing immigration policy a top priority and declined questions on the Liberia agreement [E2]. The Department of Homeland Security declined to confirm Thursday’s deportations for operational security reasons and referred questions to State [E2]. That is a non-confirmation, not a denial of the landing [E2].

Compensation is still denied in the Liberian note. The 18 August statement said the transfer is not a quid pro quo, that Liberia has not demanded or received compensation or a promise of reward, and that it will receive support to help manage the programme and strengthen its migration system [E1]. Secondary accounts of dollar amounts are not in that text [E1]. The operating fact on 20 August is the aircraft, not a new finance schedule [E2].

MICAT’s own site at the freeze still showed only the Tuesday announcement. No 20 August Liberian press release, Executive Mansion note or LINA item confirming the landing was retrieved [E1]. The arrival therefore sits on wire eyewitness copy and photographs while the government’s last signed artefact remains the 18 August promise [E1][E2]. One later count of 15, attributed to the foreign minister, is not in the AP landing account [E2].

What is still unmeasured is the nationalities of this specific 20, where they were housed after the bus left the tarmac, and the date of a second batch [E1][E2]. The 1,200 annual cap is a ceiling, not a completed flow [E1]. Thursday’s plane is the first operating print on a calendar Liberia published two days earlier [E1][E2].

evidence_box.fragment: first batch of 20 individuals to be transferred to Liberia
20 deportees arrived at Roberts International Airport
